summary_html: Child safely **reunified with parent or guardian**, case closed. Federal policy treats reunification as the preferred outcome once risk factors are mitigated.
authority_html:
- **Adoption and Safe Families Act (ASFA)** — establishes reunification timelines and permanency goals  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funds reunification services and tracks permanency outcomes

primary_citations.citation_text: Louisiana - Children’s Code Article 601 et seq. (Children’s Code – Child in Need of Care, includes reporting duties)
Louisiana - La. R.S. 46:288.1 et seq. (Extended Foster Care Program Act)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The Louisiana Supreme Court affirmed reversal of a termination judgment, holding that where reunification is the permanent plan the department must make reasonable efforts to help the parent remove the impediments to reunification - here to obtain suitable and affordable housing - before seeking termination under La. Ch.C. art. 1015(5).
key_cases.relevance: Is the leading Louisiana statement that reunification remains the primary goal and imposes an ongoing departmental duty.
key_cases.quote: the duty to make reasonable efforts to remove the impediments to reunification does not necessarily stop once the children are removed from the parent's custody

key_cases.court: Court of Appeal of Louisiana, Second Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court of appeal affirmed the change of the child's permanent plan to adoption after three adjudications, nine placements and nearly five years in foster care, holding the court must select the plan most appropriate and in the child's best interest and that the department had exceeded reasonable efforts at reunification.
key_cases.relevance: Marks the point at which reunification ceases to be the appropriate permanent plan under Louisiana law.
key_cases.quote: The court is required to determine the permanent plan for the child that is most appropriate and in the best interest of the child.

key_cases.holding: The Louisiana Supreme Court held the juvenile court exceeded its authority by ordering the department to move a child adjudicated in need of care into a certified foster home, because La. Ch.C. art. 672(A) gives the department sole authority over placement, with judicial control exercised through approval and review of the case plan.
key_cases.relevance: Frames the court's supervisory role over the plan that must move the child toward a permanent home.
key_cases.quote: the court was without authority to order the child's movement to a certified foster home

key_cases.case_name: State in the Interest of S.M.
key_cases.holding: The Louisiana Supreme Court reversed the approval of reunification as the permanency plan, holding that the record contained no evidence of a reasonable expectation of the mother's reformation in the foreseeable future and that the juvenile court abused its discretion; it remanded for an expedited hearing on a new plan.
key_cases.relevance: It is the Louisiana Supreme Court decision holding that reunification may not be approved as the permanent plan without record evidence of the parent's actual reformation, and it is the authority State ex rel. P.B. relies on for the child's right to a stable permanent home.
key_cases.quote: More than simply protecting parental rights, our judicial system is required to protect the children's rights to thrive and survive

key_cases.holding: The Louisiana Supreme Court reversed the court of appeal and reinstated the termination of a mother's parental rights, holding that the State proved a ground under La. Ch.C. art. 1015(5) by clear and convincing evidence and that leaving the children indefinitely in foster care was not in their best interests.
key_cases.relevance: It holds that permanent placement under La. Ch.C. art. 603 does not include leaving children indefinitely in foster care, which fixes the point at which reunification must give way.
key_cases.quote: In balancing these interests, the courts of this state have consistently found the interest of the child to be paramount over that of the parent

extended_foster_care_age: 18 to 21 (voluntary Extended Foster Care Program; must have been adjudicated a child in need of care and in DCFS custody the day before turning 18, plus a school, work, or medical condition; La. R.S. 46:288.2(3), 288.3)

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
